clue.text: Like cream so cooked it won't burn

parts.note: like means as, in 'as good as gold'
the cream of something is its best part

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged, like ingredients in a recipe

explanation.surface: A kitchen boast about a cream sauce so well made that it will never catch in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns SO into OS. The cookery picture makes 'cream' look like dairy, but it is the best of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was prized as a fireproof material because flames do not consume it.

clue.text: The old one is proverbially immortal

definitions.text: The old one is proverbially immortal

parts.words: The old one is proverbially immortal
parts.note: recalls the saying that old warriors never die, they only fade away

explanation.definitionFit: The song and saying 'Old soldiers never die' makes the veteran fighter proverbially deathless.

clue.text: The last person to show moderation

definitions.text: The last person to show moderation

parts.words: The last person to show moderation
parts.note: 'last' reads as least likely, and also as at the far end, where the extreme lies

explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic holds views at the far end, so moderation is the last thing such a person shows.

clue.text: Scholar's work, this, about French art

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the word this surrounds the French

parts.note: taken as written
in French tu es means 'thou art', so art is es

explanation.surface: A student's dissertation on French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb form, as in 'thou art', not painting; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A long dissertation submitted for a degree is a scholar's piece of research.

clue.text: Like an autobiography — so obvious a clue?

definitions.meaning: a life story explains its own writer, so it is about explaining oneself
so plain it needs no further explanation

explanation.walkthrough: 'a clue?' is a wry aside: the clue itself barely needs solving.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobiography is one's own account of oneself, and a plain statement needs no elucidation.

clue.text: They make a beautiful trio

parts.note: the clue points to the three sister goddesses of charm and beauty in Greek myth, often painted together

explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth three goddesses personified beauty, charm and joy, and are always shown as a trio.

clue.text: Not a good-looking eavesdropper

parts.note: eavesdropper read literally: something hanging at the eaves dropping rainwater, carved as a grotesque face

explanation.definitionFit: Ugly carved spouts on church roofs throw rainwater clear of the eaves.

clue.text: "I am the — of my soul" (Henley)

parts.note: the closing line of W E Henley's poem Invictus, 'I am the master of my fate', then this word

explanation.definitionFit: Invictus ends 'I am the master of my fate, I am the — of my soul', naming the ship's commander.

clue.text: One of them employed Dukas' apprentice

definitions.text: One of them employed Dukas' apprentice

parts.words: One of them employed Dukas' apprentice
parts.note: Paul Dukas wrote the orchestral piece about a young magician's assistant whose broom runs amok

explanation.definitionFit: Dukas's tone poem is The Sorcerer's Apprentice, so a wizard was the apprentice's master.

clue.text: Shelley hailed this spirit

parts.note: the clue recalls the opening line of Shelley's poem To a Skylark, which greets the bird as a carefree spirit

explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's To a Skylark begins 'Hail to thee, blithe Spirit!'; the missing adjective is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's first line greets the skylark with this word, meaning cheerful and carefree.

clue.text: Impulsion to frolic in the garden?

definitions.note: names a place, standing for a plant found in a garden

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the impulse word joins the end of the frolic word

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a frolic
a spur is an impulse or incentive

explanation.surface: Someone feels a sudden urge to romp about among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' puts SPUR on the end of LARK. The definition is loose: a plant one finds in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium-like flowers on tall spikes are a cottage-garden favourite.

clue.text: A long sentence ?

parts.note: not a wordy grammatical sentence but a court's punishment, the longest prison term a judge can impose

explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence keeps a prisoner locked up for the whole of their remaining years.

clue.text: Length to scale

parts.note: the stretch a musical scale covers, from one note up to the same note eight steps higher

explanation.definitionFit: A major or minor scale runs eight notes from a keynote to its repeat, that musical interval.

clue.text: Row about artist, noisy laugher It's said

definitions.note: a person laughing; the idiom names a thing laughed like

indicators.note: about means going round, so the noise word surrounds the artist

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Neighbours argue over a painter whose loud cackle is notorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The British idiom 'laugh like a drain' means to laugh loudly and coarsely, hence 'it's said'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares raucous laughter to the gurgling of water down a sewer pipe.

clue.text: Town home of a darkish horse?

indicators.note: of links the home to its owner, so the horse word comes before the home

parts.note: a dun is a horse of dull greyish-brown colour
a stable is the home of a horse

explanation.surface: A town where a rank outsider of a racehorse is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' gives the stable belonging to the dun. DUNSTABLE is a town in Bedfordshire, England. The surface plays on 'dark horse', an unknown contender.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town in Bedfordshire lies north of London.

clue.text: Device one can perhaps put in fruit

indicators.note: put in tells us these letters go inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may come out in some other order

explanation.surface: A gadget that lets you insert a single tin into a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I and CAN into IANC, and 'put in' signals it goes inside the fruit. 'can' looks like a tin but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic machine such as a washer or toaster is a household device.

clue.text: Humane tea-brewing assembly in the club

indicators.note: brewing suggests the letters are stirred and steeped into a new mixture

explanation.surface: Kindly tea-making at a gathering in a gentleman's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges HUMANETEA. The Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club; the word also means a literary institution or assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Athena's temple where poets gathered, it is a literary institution and a London club.

clue.text: Squeezes it inside the author's works

indicators.note: inside tells us the little word goes within the squeezing word

parts.note: wrings means squeezes, as with wet washing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author's output squeezes something in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeezes' reads as the subject of a sentence, but it supplies the container and 'inside' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Writings are the books and pieces a writer produces, their works.

clue.text: Like the appearances stars regularly make

definitions.text: Like the appearances stars regularly make

parts.words: Like the appearances stars regularly make
parts.note: not film stars on stage but stars in the sky, which show themselves only after dark

explanation.definitionFit: Stars are seen only at night, so their appearances belong to the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Just the one to run through a menu?

definitions.text: Just the one to run through a menu

parts.words: Just the one to run through a menu
parts.note: running through a menu suggests eating every dish, but a runner here is a swift horse, and the menu is a set of dishes

explanation.definitionFit: A swift horse is a runner, and a menu runs through dishes in turn, hence a punning runner through them.

clue.text: Reports of these but not from the Fire Station

definitions.text: Reports of these but not from the Fire Station

parts.words: Reports of these but not from the Fire Station
parts.note: a report is a bang from a gun firing, not a written report from the fire brigade, though firing is involved

explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire makes loud bangs called reports, each from a discharge of a gun.

clue.text: 2's leader escapes from most dense spinney

indicators.note: escapes from means the letter leaves the word, dropped out of it

parts.note: thickest means most dense

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so this asks for the first letter of that answer

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer to 2 down, the immortal old fighter

explanation.surface: A leader breaks out of the thickest part of a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: '2's leader' is S, the first letter of SOLDIER (2 down), and 'escapes from' drops it from THICKEST. A spinney is a British word for a small wood or copse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense patch of trees and shrubs is a small wood, a copse.

clue.text: They have time on their hands

annotationWithheld.why: They have time on their hands (6): this cryptic definition fits CLOCKS (hands showing the time), not the filed BLOCKS, and no crossing confirms either letter
annotationWithheld.clue: They have time on their hands

clue.text: It's not played at school

parts.note: sounds like a game missing from the timetable, but this is the thing pupils play when they skip lessons altogether

explanation.definitionFit: One who plays truant stays away from school without leave, so the game is never at school.

clue.text: It fills the gap between Old and New Worlds

definitions.text: It fills the gap between Old and New Worlds

parts.words: It fills the gap between Old and New Worlds
parts.note: the gap is the stretch of sea dividing Europe and Africa from the Americas

explanation.definitionFit: This ocean lies between Europe and Africa (the Old World) and the Americas (the New).

clue.text: He took the lead at Belmont

definitions.text: He took the lead at Belmont

parts.words: He took the lead at Belmont
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, Portia's suitors at Belmont choose among gold, silver and lead caskets; one suitor wins by taking lead

explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice this suitor picks the lead casket at Portia's Belmont and wins her hand.

clue.text: Controllers of the works and the weather

definitions.text: Controllers of the works and the weather

parts.words: Controllers of the works and the weather
parts.note: two job titles: an official overseeing building works, and the jocular official said to control the weather

explanation.walkthrough: A clerk of works supervises building work, and 'the clerk of the weather' is a jokey British name for whoever decides the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Office officials give their title to both the building overseer and the imaginary weather controller.

clue.text: Three rights, so 'e made out, become wrongs

parts.note: 'e is he with the H dropped, leaving the letter E

indicators.note: made out suggests the letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, and three of them give three Rs

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of turning three rights into wrongs, as he made out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' rearranges RRR, SO and E. The surface plays on the saying that two wrongs don't make a right.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakes are wrongs in the sense of things done incorrectly.

clue.text: See some yeti wandering in a national park

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters roam about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist spots a few abominable snowmen roaming a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges SOMEYETI. 'See' is a link: you will see the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous Californian park in the Sierra Nevada is protected land run by the US government.
